label: rem:em-coupling-chern-simons
title: Conjectured Chern-Simons correction form $1/\alpha = q[9]_q[10]_q\cdot\bigl(1+\delta_{CS}/(1-\delta_{CS}\kappa)\bigr)$ (Gram-determinant $\kappa$ unproved)
html:
Chern--Simons level from existence of the quantum observable universe

The Chern--Simons level k is not an independent input. The existence proof for a quantum observable universe (QOU existence) sets q = e^{\pi i/(k + h^{\vee})}. This makes \mathbf{C} = \mathbf{Rep}_{k}(\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}) the modular tensor category. This category simultaneously fixes the braiding in the Skein relation and the Chern-Simons partition function on the brane. The index k = \langle c_{2}(\mathrm{Ad}(P)), [M] \rangle determines the q-deformation of the q-dimensions [m]_{q}, [n]_{q} and the functional \mathrm{CS}(T_{m, n}) through a single Reshetikhin-Turaev construction. The numerical prediction specialises this shared object. It does not combine two independent quantities.

Conjecture (Chern-Simons descent correction, \kappa unproved). The fine structure constant receives corrections from the Chern–Simons invariants of the force-carrier torus knots T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} on Bring's surface:

  \frac{1}{\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}}
  = q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q \cdot
    \Bigl(1 + \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{CS}}}{1 - \delta_{\mathrm{CS}}\kappa}\Bigr)

The correction tower \sum_{j\ge1}\delta_{\mathrm{CS}}^{\,j}\kappa^{\,j-1} is geometric with ratio \delta_{\mathrm{CS}}\kappa \approx 2.7\times10^{-3}, so it sums in closed form and has no truncation order to choose. The order-\delta_{\mathrm{CS}}^2 form 1 + \delta_{\mathrm{CS}} + \delta_{\mathrm{CS}}^2\kappa, which this proposition previously displayed, is its second-order truncation and costs 11.06 ppb.

where:

  \delta_{\mathrm{CS}}
  = \frac{\bigl(\mathrm{CS}(T_{2,9}) + \mathrm{CS}(T_{3,5})\bigr)
              \cdot \tfrac{[2]_q}{2} \cdot \hbar_q^2}
             {q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q}

and \kappa = \det G_{\mathrm{CS}}^{\mathrm{cl}} / \det G_{\mathrm{CS}}^{q} is the Gram determinant ratio of the classical and q-deformed Chern–Simons pairing on Bring's surface.

At the proton-pinned q_0 with the Witten-1988 value \kappa \approx 1.722, 1/\alpha evaluates to 137.0359351 with the tower summed to all orders. The CODATA-2022 value is 137.035999177(21), so the residual is -468 ppb. The value \kappa = 1.722 derives from the sketched Gram-determinant computation but was admitted as sorry in the Lean formalisation (em-coupling-chern-simons.lean). It was never closed. Exact matching at this pin requires \kappa \approx 1.9153, which differs from the Witten value by 11.2\%.

Of the two candidate causes — a wrong Gram-determinant identification of \kappa, or an order-\delta_{CS}^2 truncation omitting higher-order contributions — the second is now excluded. The tower is geometric with ratio \delta_{CS}\kappa \approx 2.7\times10^{-3}, so it sums in closed form as 1 + \delta_{CS}/(1-\delta_{CS}\kappa), and the omitted orders are worth 11.06 ppb against a 468 ppb gap — roughly one part in forty. Summing them makes the residual smaller but leaves it the same size. The defect is therefore \kappa, the quantity still carried as a sorry.

Superseded figures, recorded so the change is legible: this paragraph read 137.035944 / 399 ppb against CODATA-2018, which is the order-\delta_{CS}^2 truncation at the muon pin. Resummation accounts for 11.06 ppb of the difference and the pin change for 79.17 ppb; each is invariant across the other. Reproduce with alpha_em_form_comparison_probe.py.

Proof sketch (does not close \kappa). The bare coupling \alpha = q^{-1}/([9]_q \cdot [10]_q) arises from the antisymmetric braiding eigenvalue. This is Layer 2 of EM coupling projection. It is normalized by the force-carrier q-dimensions from Layer 3.

The correction arises from the descent decomposition of the coupling endomorphism P_{\mathrm{anti}} on the force-carrier configuration. The torus knots T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} are non-hyperbolic. Their \tau-image geometric invariant is the Chern–Simons functional, not the hyperbolic volume:

  \mathrm{CS}(T_{m,n})
  = \frac{\pi^2 (m^2-1)(n^2-1)}{12 m n}.

The factor [2]_q/2 is the q-deformation of \mathrm{Vol}(S^3)/\mathrm{Vol}(S^3_{\mathrm{classical}}). It replaces \mathrm{Vol}(S^3) = 2\pi^2 with \mathrm{Vol}(S^3_q) = \pi^2 [2]_q.

At order J^2, the Gram matrix of the Chern-Simons pairing for the configuration (T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}) on Bring's surface gives:

  G_{\mathrm{CS}} =
  \begin{pmatrix}
    \mathrm{CS}_1 + \pi^2 s_1^2 / c_1^2
    & \pi^2 \ell^2 / (c_1 c_2) \\
    \pi^2 \ell^2 / (c_1 c_2)
    & \mathrm{CS}_2 + \pi^2 s_2^2 / c_2^2
  \end{pmatrix}

where s_i = (m_i-1)(n_i-1) is the self-linking, \ell = |m_1 n_2 - m_2 n_1| = 17 is the linking number, and c_i = m_i n_i is the crossing product. The q-deformed version replaces m,n with [m]_q, [n]_q.

The determinant ratio \kappa = \det G^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\mathrm{CS}} / \det G^{q}_{\mathrm{CS}} --- of the 2 \times 2 Chern--Simons pairing displayed above, not of the 6 \times 6 Markov--Gram \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) of Frobenius Gram matrix, which is a different matrix and is singular under the production trace convention --- is conjectured to capture the self-dual damping at the J^2 level, with numerical value \kappa \approx 1.722. This identification is unproved. The Gram matrix is dimensionally ambiguous. Two sources of freedom were named here: the choice of basis for the rank-2 sublattice, and the explicit form of s_i, \ell, c_i in the q-deformed setting. Neither survives examination as an explanation of the residual.

The first is not a source of freedom at all. Write B for the change of basis. A Gram matrix transforms by congruence, G \mapsto B^{\top} G B, so its determinant acquires (\det B)^2 --- the same factor on both sides of the ratio, where it cancels. Hence \kappa is independent of the basis for every invertible B, unimodular or otherwise, so no choice of rank-2 sublattice can move it (QOU.Archimedean.gramDetRatio_congr_invariant, sorry-free; confirmed numerically to 60 digits under unimodular, index-2 and irrational B).

The second is finite, and has been enumerated. Each of s_i, \ell, c_i and \mathrm{CS} admits two readings of the instruction replace m,n with [m]_q,[n]_q --- deform the composite, or deform its constituents --- giving 16 combinations, of which the shipped producer is one. Evaluated at the proton pin, \kappa ranges over [-10.92, 144.61] and none of the 16 falls inside the window [1.8739, 1.9567] that would bring 1/\alpha within 100 ppb. The shipped reading is the closest of the 16, which is what selecting for closeness would produce and is therefore not evidence that it is correct. Reproduce with alpha_em_kappa_qdeformation_family_probe.py.

This is a scope-limited negative: the [m]_q substitution family, alone, does not supply the required \kappa. It does not exclude a Gram-determinant \kappa, because a different pairing --- different matrix entries, rather than a different reading of these ones --- is untouched by the enumeration. The resulting \kappa is not computed end-to-end. A direct fit to CODATA gives \kappa \approx 1.9153 at the proton pin with the tower resummed. This sentence previously read \kappa \approx 1.8878, which is the same fit taken at the muon pin under the order-\delta_{CS}^2 truncation against CODATA-2018 (1.8877596) --- stale rather than wrong, and superseded by the resummation and re-pin recorded in the status paragraph above. Of the three explanations this paragraph has offered for the residual, two are now closed: the missing higher-order term is excluded by the resummation above, and the two named ambiguities in \kappa are excluded by the paragraphs above. What survives is the third --- that the ansatz uses the wrong decomposition, so that the pairing whose determinants are being compared is not the right one. Closing \kappa structurally remains an open problem. See open problems.\square
